$comment: The single source of truth for everything a Saathi client and the backend must agree on.
Swift, C# and TypeScript are all GENERATED from this file into each client's source tree.
Never edit a generated file: `npm run generate -w contract` rewrites them, and CI fails any PR
where the checked-in output does not match what this schema produces.
The SHAPE of this file is the decided part. The action list is still a seed — the product
questions in the root README are open. The PROVIDER section below is not a seed: running
Saathi against your own local model, with no key and no account, is the primary objective, and
the three modes here are what make that possible without a second implementation.
Why closed enums: a speech pipeline mishears. When a misheard word can only produce a wrong
VALUE inside a known set, never a wrong COMMAND, the blast radius of a mishearing stays small.

backend.$comment: Hosted is the default; a local backend is an explicit override, not the other way round.

routes.summary: Opens a companion session and returns the actions this client may perform.

config.$comment: ~/.saathi/shell.json on every platform. Owner-readable only (0600) — it can hold a key.

fields.name: provider
fields.doc: Which mode to run in. Unset means local — see providers.default.

fields.name: providerBaseUrl
fields.doc: Overrides the provider's default base URL (another Ollama host, a proxy, a compatible server).

fields.name: apiKey
fields.doc: Your own provider key, for the openai and anthropic modes. Never sent to Saathi's servers.

fields.name: backendUrl
fields.doc: Overrides the hosted backend URL. Only used in hosted mode.

fields.name: token
fields.doc: Account token for the hosted backend. Only used in hosted mode.

enums.name: ProviderKind
enums.doc: Where the model actually runs. This is the choice that decides whether anything the learner says leaves their machine.

enums.name: Tone
enums.doc: How a spoken line should sound. Accessibility-first: the companion says what is happening, and how it says it is part of the message.

enums.name: Pace
enums.doc: How fast to move through a sequence of steps. The learner sets this, not the model.

enums.name: VoiceLane
enums.doc: How a provider carries a spoken turn. Not a quality setting — a statement of what the provider can actually do, which is why it is a column in the provider table rather than a preference.

actions.name: say
actions.doc: Speak a line to the learner. The companion narrates; this is the primary action.

parameters.name: text
parameters.doc: What to say. One or two sentences.

actions.name: showStep
actions.doc: Put one step of something being learned in front of the learner, with its place in the whole.

parameters.name: title
parameters.doc: The step itself, in a few words.

parameters.name: detail
parameters.doc: One sentence of elaboration, if it helps.

parameters.name: total
parameters.doc: How many steps there are, so progress is always audible.

actions.name: openUrl
actions.doc: Open a resource in the learner's browser. http(s) only — clients MUST reject every other scheme rather than pass it to the OS.

parameters.name: url
parameters.doc: An absolute http or https URL.

$comment: One row per ProviderKind. `defaultModel` is a starting point a user can change, not a
recommendation — model names churn faster than this file should.
`keyHeader` / `keyPrefix` say how the credential is presented, as data rather than a switch
in each client. Most providers take `Authorization: Bearer <key>`; Anthropic wants its own
`x-api-key`. Adding a provider should be a row here, not a branch in Swift and another in C#.
`local` is the default when nothing is configured, and that is deliberate: the one Windows
port of the predecessor that survived was the one that needed no API key, and someone
narrating what they struggle to learn has a real reason to want it to stay on their machine.
`voice` is the same idea applied to speech. A duplex realtime socket — speech in, speech out,
one connection — is what makes a voice companion feel instant rather than operated, and the
predecessor measured it at roughly two seconds against twelve for the alternative. But only
OpenAI ships one today; Ollama has no duplex API, Anthropic has no audio API at all, and
Sarvam has excellent Indic STT and TTS without a socket to join them. So this is a capability
column, not a preference: `realtime` where the provider really has one, `chain` (speech in,
think, speech out as three steps) everywhere else. The chain lane is slower and says so out
loud. What it is not is absent — a companion whose default mode cannot be spoken to would
have the accessibility premise backwards.

rows.doc: An OpenAI-compatible server on this machine — Ollama, LM Studio, llama.cpp. No key, no account, nothing leaves the device.
Your own OpenAI key, held on your machine and sent straight to OpenAI. Saathi's servers are not involved.
Your own Anthropic key, held on your machine and sent straight to Anthropic. Saathi's servers are not involved.
Your own Sarvam AI key, sent straight to Sarvam. Indian-built models with real Indic-language coverage — the reason this option exists, given where Saathi starts.
Saathi's hosted backend holds the provider keys; you hold an account token. For people who would rather not run or configure anything.
